page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with the running head and page number at the top. No printed marginal notes. Handwritten ink marks in the right margin are not printed and are left out. Catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: beat.R.Quia instrumentum est, apparatus rerum diutius mansurarum, sine quibus e-xerceri possefsio non poteft: frumentum autem confumitur. F. Imò instrumētum est, quodcunque ad colédum a-grum pertinet.Cultorum autem sine cibarijs nullus est u-sus. D.An instrumēti legato, cibaria cultoribus parata con-tineantur. Seruius & Vlpia-nus contineri respondent, in L.quæsitum,12. D.de inst. uel inst.Ad uerbi controuersiam illa quoque militis caussa pertinet,de qua Cicero lib.de O-rat. primo his scribit uerbis: Quæ potuit igitur esse caus-«

page.notes: The signature "n" and the catchword "fa" are read from the foot of the page and are doubtful; "n" in particular is uncertain. Several handwritten ink marks in the right margin (beside "inst.Ad uerbi") are not printed and are left out. The line "illa quoque militis caussa per tinet" is set as printed: "per" ends a line and "tinet" begins the next. The word "pertinet" is therefore given as "caussa per tinet" in the original and is transcribed here with "pertinet" joined, which the scan's line break supports. Long s has been written as plain s throughout. The printed hyphens in "e-xerceri", "a-grum", "u-sus", "con-tineantur", "Vlpia-nus", "O-rat." and "caus-" are kept.
